newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk tanker to begin loading Iraqi oil on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Turk tanker to begin loading Iraqi oil on Monday.

text.p: Loading of the first tanker of Iraqi crude to be exported through Turkey for six years will begin on Monday morning at the southern Turkish port of Ceyhan, Anatolian news agency said on Sunday.

Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan and Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller are expected to jointly press the button to begin loading at a ceremony starting at 11 a.m. (0900 GMT), the ceremony organisers, pipeline company BOTAS, said on Sunday.
The tanker is to transport crude to Turkey's state refiner Tupras' Aliaga refinery in the western city of Izmir.

Tupras has a contract with Iraq, approved by the United Nations, to buy 75,000 barrels per day under a U.N. deal which allows Iraq to sell crude in order to buy food, medicine and other humanitarian supplies.
